E1.evidence: Issue #338 "Add queue_size for publishers." (maintainer jihoonl, 2014-08-08): "for indigo", closed with the commits that add `queue_size=10` to every rospy.Publisher(...) call (f0e021c and 52aca4c for kobuki_testsuite, dd40270 "add queue_size on publiehrs #338" for kobuki_node/scripts/getOdom2D.py and getYaw.py). The defect is concrete in code: at 0.6.1 the scripts call `rospy.Publisher("pose2d", Pose2D)`, `rospy.Publisher("angle", Float64)` and `rospy.Publisher("angle_rate", Float64)` without the keyword that indigo's rospy requires, and the provider's code (ros_comm 1.11.8, rospy/topics.py) states the consequence (a SyntaxWarning and synchronous publishing). No run log is posted in the issue.

E2.evidence: Unit 1: kobuki_node's Python helper nodes getOdom2D.py and getYaw.py (installed programs of the kobuki_node package). Unit 2: rospy, the client library from ros_comm, a separately released package. The failure depends on the peer: the same calls are silent on hydro's rospy (Publisher.__init__ has no queue_size parameter at ros_comm 1.9.55) and warn on indigo's rospy (queue_size added to the signature, warning when omitted), so it is not internal (step 2); no launch/config name binding (step 3); the resolving change is an edit of the consumer's API call, not a build-system change (step 4); not firmware (step 5). Interface kind: library API (rospy.Publisher constructor).

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the scripts (added 2012-07-11, fuerte era, carried unchanged through hydro) reference rospy.Publisher as declared before ros_comm 1.11 (no queue_size parameter); the provider under indigo (ros_comm 1.11.x) runs at a newer revision whose Publisher.__init__ declares queue_size and warns when it is missing. The issue's only context is "for indigo".

E4.evidence: Code-level statement of the mismatch in the provider at the running revision: rospy/topics.py 1.11.8, Publisher.__init__: `if queue_size is not None: self.impl.set_queue_size(queue_size) else: import warnings; warnings.warn("The publisher should be created with an explicit keyword argument 'queue_size'. " "Please see http://wiki.ros.org/rospy/Overview/Publishers%20and%20Subscribers for more information.", SyntaxWarning, stacklevel=2)`, and its docstring: "When the keyword is not being used or when None is passed all publishing will happen synchronously and a warning message will be printed." The issue thread itself shows no output.

units.name: kobuki_node
units.revision_basis: The reporter names only the distro (indigo) on 2014-08-08. Tag 0.6.1 (2014-08-08, kobuki_node version 0.6.1) is an ancestor of the fix's parent 8c30446 and its kobuki_node/scripts are byte-identical to that parent (the intervening commits touch only kobuki_testsuite); the fix dd40270 (2014-08-11) is three commits before tag 0.6.2 (2014-08-11), which contains the queue_size arguments.

units.name: rospy
units.revision_basis: The reporter names only the distro. 1.11.8 (tagged 2014-08-04) was the newest indigo ros_comm release at the issue date (the next, 1.11.9, came later); the Publisher queue_size parameter and the warning for its absence are present in every indigo tag from 1.11.1 (2014-05-07) through 1.11.8 and absent in 1.11.0 and in all hydro 1.9.x tags. The resolution does not change rospy, so resolved_rev keeps the broken revision.

loudness_evidence: Diagnostic from the provider at publisher construction (node activation): rospy 1.11.8 topics.py lines 792-794 emit `SyntaxWarning: The publisher should be created with an explicit keyword argument 'queue_size'. Please see http://wiki.ros.org/rospy/Overview/Publishers%20and%20Subscribers for more information.` whenever queue_size is omitted (https://github.com/ros/ros_comm/blob/1.11.8/clients/rospy/src/rospy/topics.py#L789-L794). The composition keeps working (publishing falls back to synchronous mode per the docstring). The issue thread contains no captured output; the evidence is the provider's code, not a posted log.

resolution.summary: Commit dd40270 adds `queue_size=10` to the three rospy.Publisher calls in kobuki_node/scripts/getOdom2D.py ("pose2d") and getYaw.py ("angle", "angle_rate"), matching the indigo rospy signature; rospy is unchanged.
resolution.evidence: The fix is committed and the issue closed by the maintainer with links to the commits (https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki/issues/338#issuecomment-51578196, #issuecomment-51741633); no run of the changed scripts under indigo rospy is shown.

notes: consumer_built_against is inferred from the consumer's references: the scripts call rospy.Publisher(name, data_class) with no queue_size, matching Publisher.__init__ as declared at ros_comm 1.9.55 (`def __init__(self, name, data_class, subscriber_listener=None, tcp_nodelay=False, latch=False, headers=None)`, the last hydro release before the indigo line) and every earlier release back to the scripts' creation (2012-07-11, fuerte); 1.9.55 is used as the label because the kobuki indigo branch inherits the scripts unchanged from the hydro line. After the fix the scripts use the queue_size keyword that exists only from 1.11.1, so the resolved built-against label is the running revision 1.11.8. The condition is element_retyped: rospy.Publisher is still present, its constructor declaration changed (new queue_size parameter with a deprecation-style warning and a behavioural change to synchronous publishing when omitted). The same provider change was addressed for other consumers in the same issue, kobuki_testsuite's motion_rotate.py, motion_travel_forward.py, motion_wander.py (f0e021c) and drift_estimation.py (52aca4c); those are separate compositions, not conditions of this case. Loudness is recorded as loud_documented on the strength of the provider's source (the warning is emitted by existing tooling at activation); if only posted logs count, it should be read as unknown.
